q: What is the capital city of Scotland?
fact: Edinburgh Castle sits on top of an extinct volcano known as Castle Rock.

q: What is the capital city of Wales?
fact: Cardiff only became a city in 1905 and was named the capital of Wales in 1955.

q: What is the capital city of Northern Ireland?
fact: Belfast's giant yellow shipyard cranes are nicknamed Samson and Goliath.

q: Which river flows through the centre of London?
fact: The Thames once froze so solidly that 'frost fairs' were held on the ice.

q: The bell known as Big Ben hangs in a tower at which London building?
fact: Big Ben weighs more than 13 tonnes and began striking the hours in 1859.

q: Which London palace is the monarch's official London home?
fact: Buckingham Palace has 775 rooms, including 78 bathrooms.

q: Which vegetable is a national emblem of Wales?
fact: Many people in Wales wear a leek or a daffodil on St David's Day, 1 March.

q: Which prickly purple flower is the national emblem of Scotland?
fact: A thistle appears on the badge of Scotland's national rugby team.

q: Which flower is the national emblem of England?
fact: England's rugby team wears a red rose on its shirts.

q: What colour are London's famous double-decker buses?
fact: The classic Routemaster bus first carried London passengers in 1956.

q: What is the London Underground's famous nickname?
fact: Opened in 1863, the London Underground is the world's oldest underground railway.

q: What is the name of the giant observation wheel on London's South Bank?
fact: The London Eye was built to celebrate the new millennium and opened to the public in 2000.

q: Which creature appears on the national flag of Wales?
fact: Wales isn't represented on the Union Flag, as it was already joined to England when the flag was created.

q: Which London stadium hosts England football matches and the FA Cup Final?
fact: The giant arch over the new Wembley Stadium is 133 metres high.

q: What is the UK's flag commonly called?
fact: The Union Flag combines the crosses of St George, St Andrew and St Patrick.

q: Which northern English city is home to both United and City football clubs?
fact: Manchester's symbol, the worker bee, celebrates the city's busy industrial past.

q: Which stretch of sea separates England from France?
fact: At its narrowest point, the Strait of Dover, the Channel is only about 33 kilometres wide.

q: Which train service runs through the Channel Tunnel from London to Paris?
fact: Eurostar trains leave London from St Pancras International station.

q: The famous White Cliffs stand beside which Kent port?
fact: The White Cliffs are made of chalk, formed from the remains of tiny sea creatures.

q: Which stretch of sea lies between Great Britain and Ireland?
fact: The Isle of Man sits in the middle of the Irish Sea.

q: What is the knee-length tartan garment traditionally worn by Scottish men?
fact: Many tartan patterns are linked to a particular Scottish clan or family.

q: Which musical instrument is most closely linked with Scotland?
fact: Bagpipes get their sound from a bag of air squeezed under the player's arm.

q: Which Scottish dish is traditionally eaten on Burns Night?
fact: Burns Night celebrates the poet Robert Burns, who wrote a poem called 'Address to a Haggis'.

q: In which university city can you go punting on the River Cam?
fact: Cambridge's Mathematical Bridge is a famous wooden footbridge over the River Cam.

q: What are the ceremonial guards at the Tower of London popularly called?
fact: Officially called Yeoman Warders, Beefeaters live with their families inside the Tower.

q: Which birds are famously kept at the Tower of London?
fact: Legend says the kingdom will fall if the ravens ever leave the Tower.

q: Which London area is famous for its theatres and musicals?
fact: The site of the Theatre Royal, Drury Lane, has had a theatre on it since 1663.

q: Which London museum is famous for its dinosaur skeletons?
fact: A blue whale skeleton nicknamed Hope hangs in the Natural History Museum's main hall.

q: Which ceremony outside Buckingham Palace sees soldiers in bearskin hats swap duty?
fact: The Changing of the Guard is free to watch and draws big crowds of visitors.

q: Which national park in Cumbria is famous for its lakes and fells?
fact: England's highest mountain, Scafell Pike, is in the Lake District.

q: What is the highest mountain in Wales?
fact: A mountain railway has carried visitors up Yr Wyddfa since 1896.

q: Which Somerset festival is one of the world's most famous music festivals?
fact: Glastonbury Festival takes place on a working dairy farm called Worthy Farm.

q: Which Lancashire seaside town is famous for its tower and illuminations?
fact: Blackpool Tower was inspired by the Eiffel Tower and opened in 1894.

q: Which East Sussex seaside city is famous for its pier and Royal Pavilion?
fact: Brighton's Royal Pavilion was built as a seaside palace for the Prince Regent, later King George IV.

q: Which Yorkshire city is famous for its great Minster and old city walls?
fact: The Shambles in York is a narrow medieval street once lined with butchers' shops.
